prompt:
Isometric technical illustration, orthographic camera from one corner looking down 30 degrees, no perspective. Hairline even-weight linework on every edge. Flat four-tone shading by face direction, top faces lightest. Warm paper background for day scenes, dark navy-charcoal for night. Only parts that show live data are brass, and each carries fine engraved scale marks; every other material follows the scene's architectural tradition. Exactly one part highlighted in vivid orange: the place where value is moving right now. Engineering-drawing precision with dense, purposeful detail. Calm, legible and serious, like a plate in an engineering atlas.

One carefully designed small token stall in a canal-town market hall, shown as a single freestanding stand with a grounded base. It has a miniature self-recording tide gauge: a brass float in an engraved stilling well, fine major and minor scale ticks, and a linked pen on a small paper drum. A blank name plate and a simple invented geometric emblem are printed on physical signage. Brick, timber, enamel and riveted steel establish the canal town's material tradition. One tiny faceless automaton figure with a geometric chest emblem stands beside the stall. A miniature channel pours liquidity through the stall's small market instrument; that single connected pour is the orange part.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create one complete standalone reference candidate, not a sheet, montage or collage. Night on flat dark navy-charcoal, with crisp quiet pale linework and four distinct face tones; no lighting effects or luminous windows. Square composition; the whole subject is visible with useful breathing room. Explore a compact timber kiosk with a shallow pitched roof, a steel counter inset and a small brick footing. Integrate the miniature gauge into a narrow side bay; keep the blank enamel plate and geometric emblem physically attached. Every parallel construction edge stays parallel; equally sized elements keep equal image size at every depth. Ground joints use a quiet lighter line tone than structures. Keep face tones clearly separated, with top faces darker than the ground in day scenes. Brass is muted gold, confined to scaled instruments. Orange forms exactly one connected active part. Do not add titles, candidate labels, decorative borders or any extra interface.

Strict projection and paint discipline: use parallel axonometric projection with no focal-length camera. Every edge along the same construction axis shares exactly one angle; there is no taper, foreshortening with distance or size falloff. This reinforces the source orthographic and flat-four-tone requirements.
